issue_context.title: RESTful Integration - not working correctly with multiple resources
issue_context.body:
### The problem

As shown in the documentation, the RESTful integration can be used to capture multiple sensors from a single resource, but you can also list multiple resources to use - see the example on the documentation page, which shows two URL resources and three sensors for each one.

I'm trying to use multiple resources, and in doing so I get duplicated sensor names, not the ones I am expressly asking for.

### What is version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2021.3.0

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant Container

### Integration causing the issue

RESTful

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/rest/

### Example YAML snippet

```yaml
rest:
  - resource: https://api.covidactnow.org/v2/state/OH.json?apiKey=[key]
    scan_interval: 3600
    sensor:
      - name: "Ohio Positivity Percentage"
        value_template: '{{ "%0.1f" | format(value_json.metrics.testPositivityRatio * 100) }}'
        unit_of_measurement: '%'

  - resource: https://api.covidactnow.org/v2/county/39041.json?apiKey=[key]
    scan_interval: 3600
    sensor:
      - name: "DelCo Positivity Percentage"
        value_template: '{{ "%0.1f" | format(value_json.metrics.testPositivityRatio * 100) }}'
        unit_of_measurement: '%'
```


### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

There are no messages in the log related to this integration.


The YAML snippet above should result in two sensors, one named "Ohio Positivity Percentage" (sensor.ohio_positivity_percentage), and the other named "DelCo Positivity Percentage" (sensor.delco_positivity_percentage).

Instead I get two sensors, both named "DelCo Positivity Percentage" but with disambiguated entity names: sensor.delco_positivity_percentage and sensor.delco_positivity_percentage_2.  The first one (without the _2 suffix) contains the value from the one that **should** be named "Ohio Positivity Percentage."

The sensors **do** seem to be working correctly and the captured values are distinct.

The attached screenshot shows the entities that result from the YAML pasted above.

![Screenshot from 2021-03-13 15-35-28](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/945097/111044964-9e4fa280-8419-11eb-8b5d-39e23b1fb14c.png)
comments:
Here is a simpler example with a public API so anyone can test:

```yaml
  - resource: http://date.jsontest.com
    scan_interval: 3600
    sensor:
      - name: "JSON Date"
        value_template: '{{ value_json.date }}'
  - resource: http://time.jsontest.com
    scan_interval: 3600
    sensor:
      - name: "JSON Time"
        value_template: '{{ value_json.time }}'
```

Yields:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/945097/111221053-6333a780-85b0-11eb-8f7c-1647a0eb4a27.png)

And the actual data looks like this (for both URLs):

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/945097/111221191-8c543800-85b0-11eb-9dee-8200292a4f0c.png)

(Obviously the timestamp is different, but the YAML **should** return the date in sensor.json_date, and the time in sensor.json_time.)
@bdraco I hope you don't mind me tagging you here because this looks related to last month's refactoring of the REST integration, #46711.
Thanks!  I'll test when 2021.3.5 comes out.
Never mind - I manually updated my container image and tested.  Works great! 💯
